FeatureFlags.description:
Per-tenant feature gates.

Each flag controls whether a behaviour or UI module is active for the
tenant. Backwards-compatible defaults (`deliveries_enabled=True` and
`multi_trip_enabled=True`) preserve existing tenants' behaviour.

Adding a new flag here:
  1. Pick a sensible default (off for opt-in features, on for things
     existing tenants already get).
  2. The schema-driven settings UI picks it up automatically via
     `feature_flags_schema()` below.
  3. Runtime gates: read via `policy.feature_flags.<flag_name>` —
     never hardcode the default at the call site.
FeatureFlags.title: FeatureFlags

RecurrenceCadence.description:
How frequently the template fires.

`interval_days` is consulted for `CUSTOM` only; the other values are
self-describing.  WEEKLY honours `day_of_week_mask` (bitmask Mon=1<<0 ..
Sun=1<<6); MONTHLY honours `day_of_month` (1-31, capped at month length).
BIWEEKLY is "every 14 days from `start_date`".
RecurrenceCadence.title: RecurrenceCadence

post.description:
Directly assign all PENDING orders for target_date to couriers via VRP solver.

Unlike /optimize and /optimize/preview, this endpoint:
- Always runs with draft=False (orders go straight to ASSIGNED — no review step)
- Includes all order types (ON_DEMAND, SCHEDULED, BULK, REVERSE)
- Scopes to the given calendar day only
- Re-running is safe: already-assigned orders are untouched

parameters.description: Target date (ISO-8601, e.g. 2026-04-12). All PENDING orders with earliest_delivery on this date will be assigned to online couriers.
parameters.name: target_date

schema.description: Target date (ISO-8601, e.g. 2026-04-12). All PENDING orders with earliest_delivery on this date will be assigned to online couriers.
schema.title: Target Date

post.summary: Optimally assign all pending orders for a specific date

post.description:
Run the range planner across [date_from, date_to] inclusive.

Unlike `/dispatch/assign-optimal`, this endpoint:

  * Solves the entire range as **one** VRP, so the optimiser is free
    to swap delivery dates across days when an order's
    `[earliest_delivery, latest_delivery]` window allows it.
  * Honours every order constraint: time windows, weight/volume,
    fragile/temp-sensitive flags, and OSRM vehicle profiles.
  * Returns a celery task id you can poll via
    `GET /dispatch/optimize/{task_id}/status`, identical to the daily flow.

Re-running for an overlapping range is safe: existing PLANNED/DRAFT route
assignments inside the range are reset first, while work already in
progress or completed is left untouched.

parameters.description: Inclusive start date (ISO-8601). The solver may schedule eligible work from this day onwards.
parameters.name: date_from

schema.description: Inclusive start date (ISO-8601). The solver may schedule eligible work from this day onwards.
schema.title: Date From

parameters.description: Inclusive end date (ISO-8601). Range is capped at 14 days; longer spans return 422.
parameters.name: date_to

schema.description: Inclusive end date (ISO-8601). Range is capped at 14 days; longer spans return 422.
schema.title: Date To

post.summary: Optimally assign all pending orders across a date range (1-14 days)

post.description:
Slot a single PENDING order into the best available route using the
insertion heuristic — without touching any already-assigned orders.

Unlike /assign-optimal this does NOT re-run the full VRP solver and does
NOT disturb existing routes.  It finds the cheapest feasible insertion
point across all active courier routes and slots the order in.  If no
existing route can absorb the order a new single-order route is created
for the closest available courier.

Returns synchronously (no task polling needed).
post.summary: Insert a single PENDING order into the best available existing route
